article_title: Effectiveness of tailored educational content on improving nurses' clinical performance in cardiac surgery wards: a mixed-methods study.
citation: Kazemi-Arpanahi, H. et al. (2025). Effectiveness of tailored educational content on improving nurses’ clinical performance in cardiac surgery wards: a mixed-methods study. Scientific Reports 15, 23616. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-08728-2
title: 72-hour tailored training program combining in-person theoretical sessions with hospital-based simulation
description: The training program consisted of theoretical and practical components tailored to the 21 identified educational topics. The article describes that "the training consisted of theoretical and practical sessions, which lasted for 72 h in total", with 20 in-person sessions of 3.5 h each followed by simulation-based practical training in the hospital. Nurses had to score above 70 on a final exam to advance; 30 of 35 participants passed.
requirements: Full-time attendance, a bachelor's degree in nursing, at least 3 years of cardiac surgery ward experience, and a final exam score over 70 to qualify for the performance comparison
constraints: Five of the 35 case-group nurses failed to pass the training course and did not advance
target_learners: registered nurses with at least 3 years of C-ICU experience
target_learning_goals: clinical and diagnostic skills for cardiac surgery care, including reducing cardiac surgery complications
examples: Theoretical training covered cardiac surgery topics in 20 in-person sessions; practical training used simulations in the hospital to enhance clinical and diagnostic skills
key_sources: Kazemi-Arpanahi, H. et al. (2025). Effectiveness of tailored educational content on improving nurses’ clinical performance in cardiac surgery wards: a mixed-methods study. Scientific Reports 15, 23616. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-08728-2
